title: End the VAT relief on Motability cars
headline: End the Motability VAT relief: HMRC’s £1.5bn, less what Budget 2025 took: £1.2bn.
description: Cars leased to disabled people through the Motability scheme are zero-rated for VAT. HMRC costs that relief at £1.49 billion in 2025-26. Budget 2025 already charged VAT on advance payments and insurance premium tax on the leases’ insurance, worth £280 million by 2029-30, so ending the rest of the relief is worth about £1.2 billion, the figure Onward and the Adam Smith Institute quote. Static, and held flat in cash.

baselinePolicy.text: Vehicles supplied to disabled people under the Motability scheme are zero-rated for VAT; from July 2026 VAT is charged on advance payments and insurance premium tax on the related insurance.

source.quote: Motability: Introduce VAT at the standard rate on Advance Payments paid to Motability or equivalent schemes, and Insurance Premium Tax at the standard rate on insurance related to vehicle leases, from 1 July 2026

alreadyIncludes: Budget 2025 line 14: VAT on advance payments and IPT on lease insurance from 1 July 2026 (£280 million in 2029-30).

terms.label: HMRC’s cost of the VAT zero rate on vehicles for disabled people, 2025-26

source.note: row vat-ns15 of the extract: "Vehicles and other supplies to disabled people [vehicles only]"

terms.label: What Budget 2025 already takes from the same scheme in 2029-30, netted off

source.quote: Motability: Introduce VAT at the standard rate on Advance Payments paid to Motability or equivalent schemes, and Insurance Premium Tax at the standard rate on insurance related to vehicle leases, from 1 July 2026

rawSource.note: HMRC’s 2025-26 relief cost less the Budget 2025 line already scored on the scheme, held flat in cash from the start year. The netting is approximate: HMRC’s row is the whole zero rate on vehicles and the scorecard line includes insurance premium tax.

caveats: Static: HMRC says the cost of a relief is not the yield from removing it. Fewer people would lease through the scheme, and cheaper cars would be chosen.

The netting is approximate: HMRC’s row covers vehicles supplied to disabled people generally, and the Budget 2025 line includes insurance premium tax as well as VAT. Onward and the Adam Smith Institute quote the £1.2 billion.
The relief is a benefit to disabled people in kind; ending it raises the cost of a Motability lease by a fifth.

considerations.text: HMRC’s relief cost is not the yield from ending it: with VAT at 20%, some of the 800,000-odd scheme customers would lease cheaper cars or leave the scheme, and the yield would fall short of the static figure.
Disabled people who lease a car with the mobility part of their PIP or DLA; Onward argues the scheme’s bespoke reliefs cost taxpayers £1.2 billion a year and should go.

sources.quote: the Chancellor should have removed Motability’s bespoke tax reliefs, which cost taxpayers £1.2 billion per year
